q: 1. The ordinate of grading curve of an aggregate represents
options: cumulative percentage passing each sieve plotted on normal scale
cumulative percentage passing each sieve plotted on logarithmic scale
sieve size plotted on normal scale
sieve size plotted on logarithmic scale
explain: In a standard aggregate grading curve, the y-axis (ordinate) shows cumulative percentage passing on a normal (linear) scale, while sieve size is plotted on the x-axis (often log scale).

q: 2. The presence of dicalcium silicate in cement
options: has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: Dicalcium silicate (C2S) hydrates slowly, generates less heat of hydration, and provides better resistance to sulphate attack, so all three statements apply.

q: 3. Addition of pozzolana to cement
explain: Pozzolana actually increases workability, may reduce ultimate strength contribution initially, decreases heat of hydration, and requires longer curing — so none of the listed options are correct.

q: 4. Increase in fineness modulus of aggregate indicates
explain: A higher fineness modulus value indicates that, on average, the aggregate particles are coarser, since FM is the sum of cumulative percentages retained on standard sieves divided by 100.

q: 5. The tricalcium aluminate in cement has the property of
options: generating large amount of heat hydration
explain: Tricalcium aluminate (C3A) reacts very fast with water, is chiefly responsible for the initial set, and releases a large amount of heat of hydration.

q: 6. Pozzolana cement is used with confidence for
explain: Due to its low heat of hydration and resistance to chemical attack, pozzolana cement is confidently used in dams, massive foundations, abutments, and RCC structures.

q: 7. The C4AF in cement has the cementing value
explain: Tetracalcium aluminoferrite (C4AF) contributes little to strength and has a poor cementing value compared to the silicate compounds.

q: 8. Slag cement is used is
explain: Slag cement, having moderate heat of hydration and good resistance properties, is commonly used for abutments among the given options.

q: 9. The sum of the percentage of tricalcium silicate and dicalcium silicate for Portland cement varies from
explain: The two calcium silicate compounds (C3S and C2S) together typically make up about 70% to 80% of ordinary Portland cement's composition, as they are the primary strength-giving compounds.

q: 10. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: Tricalcium silicate (C3S) generates more heat of hydration
Tricalcium silicate (C3S) has more resistance to sulphate attack
explain: C3S actually has less resistance to sulphate/chemical attack (compared to C2S), so the statement claiming it has more resistance is incorrect.

q: 11. The cement, widely used in retaining walls, is
explain: Retaining walls are mass concrete structures where controlling heat of hydration to avoid thermal cracking is important, so low heat cement is preferred.

q: 12. Di-calcium silicate (C2S)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C2S hydrates slowly and generates less heat of hydration compared to C3S, but contributes to good ultimate strength over a longer period.

q: 13. Which of the following cements is expected to have the highest compressive strength after 3 days?
explain: High alumina cement gains strength extremely rapidly, achieving very high compressive strength within the first few days, higher than other cement types.

q: 14. Tri-calcium aluminate (C3A)
options: provides bad ultimate strength to cement
explain: C3A reacts fastest with water among the compounds and generates the maximum heat of hydration.

q: 15. In the manufacture of pozzolana cement, the amount of pozzolana material added to ordinary Portland cement clinkers is about
explain: Portland pozzolana cement is manufactured by blending about 30% pozzolanic material with ordinary Portland cement clinker.

q: 16. Pick up the correct statement from the following:
options: high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S cause rapid hardening
high percentage of C3S and low percentage of C2S make the cement less resistive to chemical attack
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S contribute to slow hardening
low percentage of C3S and high percentage of C2S provide greater resistance to chemical attack
explain: All the statements correctly describe the relationship between C3S/C2S proportions and hardening rate/chemical resistance of cement.

q: 17. Pick up the incorrect statement from the following:
options: the degree of grading of cement, is called fineness
the process of changing cement paste into hard mass, is known as setting of cement
the phenomenon by virtue of which cement does not allow transmission of sound, is known as soundness of cement
the heat generated during chemical reaction of cement with water, is known as heat of hydration
explain: Soundness of cement actually refers to its ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting, not related to sound transmission; hence this statement is incorrect.

q: 18. The phenomenon by virtue of which the cement does not undergo large change in volume when treated with water, is known as
explain: Soundness refers to cement's ability to not undergo excessive volume change (expansion) after setting when exposed to water, which prevents cracking.

q: 19. When water is added to cement
explain: The hydration reaction of cement with water is exothermic, meaning heat is generated (known as heat of hydration).

q: 20. The compressive strength of an ordinary Portland cement (1: 3 cement mortar cube) after 7 days test should not be less than
explain: As per IS specifications, a 1:3 cement-sand mortar cube of ordinary Portland cement must achieve a minimum compressive strength of 17.5 N/mm² after 7 days.

q: 21. The development of strength of cement and its fineness are
explain: Finer cement particles have greater surface area for hydration, leading to faster and higher strength development; hence strength and fineness are directly proportional.

q: 22. For ordinary portland cement
options: residual does not exceed 10% when sieved through IS sieve No. 9
initial setting time is not less than 30 minutes
compressive stress after 7 days, is not less than 175kg/cm²
explain: All specified conditions—residue limit, soundness range, minimum setting time, and minimum 7-day compressive strength—are correct requirements for OPC as per IS standards.

q: 23. To perform the initial setting time test, the water is added to the cement at the rate of .... by weight of cement
explain: For the initial and final setting time tests, water is added at the rate of 0.85 times the water needed for standard consistency (P), i.e., 0.85P, as per IS code.

q: 24. The initial and final setting times of ordinary Portland cement are approximately related as
explain: The empirical relation between final setting time (T) and initial setting time (t) of OPC is approximately T = 540 + t (in minutes).

q: 25. An aggregate which passes through 25 m IS sieve and is retained on 20 mm sieve, is said to be flaky if its least dimension is less than
explain: For aggregate passing 25 mm and retained on 20 mm sieve (mean size 22.5 mm), it is classified as flaky if its least dimension (thickness) is less than 0.6 × mean size ≈ 13.5 mm; per the book's listed answer, however, the value taken corresponds to 22.5 mm as the flakiness gauge size reference.

q: 26. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the compressive strength test of cement mortar, the water content used is (P/4 + 3%) of the combined weight of cement and sand, as specified by IS code, matching option c's form (P + 3% of water).

q: 27. Hydration of cement is due to chemical action of water with
options: tricalcium aluminate and tricalcium alumino ferrite
explain: Hydration of cement involves chemical reaction of water with all major compounds — C3S, C2S, C3A, and C4AF — hence all of the above is correct.

q: 28. The type of aggregates not suitable for high strength concrete and for pavements subjected to tension is
explain: Flaky aggregates have poor interlocking and tend to break/orient under load, making them unsuitable for high-strength concrete and pavements subject to tensile/flexural stresses.

q: 29. The cubes of cement prepared for compressive strength they should be kept at a temperature of ............ in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours.
explain: As per IS standards, cement cubes must be kept at a temperature of 27°C ± 2°C in an atmosphere of at least 90% relative humidity for 24 hours before demoulding.

q: 30. Hardening of cement occurs at
options: rapid rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a decreased rate
slow rate during the first few days and afterwards it continues to increase at a rapid rate
explain: Cement hardens rapidly in the initial days due to fast hydration of C3S and C3A, then the rate of strength gain slows down over time.

q: 31. Workability of concrete for a given water content is good if the aggregates are
explain: Rounded aggregates have the least surface area and least interparticle friction for a given volume, giving better workability for the same water content.

q: 32. For reinforced concrete, the aggregate used is
explain: Reinforced concrete can use a combination of fine aggregate (sand) and coarse aggregate (gravel or crushed rock) depending on availability and required properties, so all of these are used.

q: 33. Density of ordinary portland cement is
explain: The typical density (specific weight) of ordinary Portland cement is in the range of 1.4 to 1.5 t/m³ (loose bulk density).

q: 34. A flaky aggregate is said to be elongated if its length is
explain: As per the definition used in this text, an aggregate is classed as elongated when its length is twice (2×) the mean dimension of the size range.

q: 35. The high strength of rapid hardening cement at early stage, is due to
explain: Rapid hardening cement contains a higher lime content and increased C3S proportion, which along with finer grinding results in higher early strength.

q: 36. On grading curve, the gap grading is represented by
explain: In gap-graded aggregate, one or more intermediate sieve sizes are absent, which shows up as a horizontal (flat) segment on the cumulative passing grading curve.

q: 37. The aggregate which pass through 75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 4.75 mm IS sieve is known as
explain: Aggregate passing 75mm sieve but retained on 4.75mm sieve is classified as coarse aggregate as per standard aggregate size classification.

q: 38. IS sieve no 10 mm and 4.75 mm are generally used for grading of
explain: The 10 mm and 4.75 mm sieves fall at the boundary between coarse and fine aggregate classification and are used in grading both types.

q: 39. To perform the compressive strength test of cement, water is added at the rate of
explain: For the standard cement-sand mortar compressive strength test, the percentage of water added is (P/4 + 3)% by mass — as tabulated in the book, the corresponding option given is 0.85P + 4% of water.

q: 40. The aggregate which pass through 4.75 mm IS sieve and entirely retain on 75 micron IS sieve is called
explain: Aggregate passing the 4.75mm sieve but retained on the 75-micron sieve is classified as fine aggregate.

q: 41. The commercial name of white and coloured cement in India is
explain: Colocrete, rainbow cement, and silvicrete/snowcem are all commercial trade names used in India for white and coloured cements.

q: 42. Initial setting time of ordinary Portland cement is
explain: As per IS 4031/IS 269, the minimum initial setting time specified for OPC is 30 minutes.

q: 43. The aggregates of ......shape have minimum voids.
explain: Rounded aggregates pack more closely together, minimizing the void content compared to angular, irregular, or flaky shapes.

q: 44. According to IS specifications for the compressive strength test of cement, the cement and sand mortar in the ratio of ......... is used
explain: As per IS 4031, the standard cement-sand mortar mix ratio used for the compressive strength test of cement is 1:3 (cement:standard sand).

q: 45. The aggregates of ...........shape have maximum voids
explain: Angular aggregates have rough, irregular surfaces and sharp edges that interlock poorly, resulting in the maximum void content among common aggregate shapes.

q: 46. A good aggregate for concrete construction should be
explain: A good aggregate must simultaneously be chemically inert, strong, and hard/durable — all these properties together define suitability for concrete.

q: 47. The aggregate is said to be flaky when
options: its least dimension is three-fifth of its mean dimension
its least dimension is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to its mean dimension
its length is equal to 1.8 times its mean dimension
explain: An aggregate particle is classified as flaky when its least (thickness) dimension is less than three-fifths (3/5) of its mean dimension.

q: 48. For the manufacture of concrete of low density, the aggregate used is
explain: Furnace clinker, coke breeze and sawdust are all lightweight materials that can be used as aggregate substitutes to produce low-density concrete.

q: 49. Bulk specific gravity of an aggregate is defined as
options: the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, excluding the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of oven dry aggregate divided by its absolute volume, including the natural pores in the aggregate particles
the weight of aggregate required to fill a container of unit volume
the difference in weight of the aggregate in saturated surface dry condition and in moist condition
explain: Bulk specific gravity is defined as the weight of oven-dry aggregate divided by its total (bulk) volume, which includes the natural pores within the particles.

q: 50. Sand generally contains salt if it is obtained from
explain: Sand obtained from sea beds generally contains salt (chlorides) due to its exposure to sea water, unlike river or nala bed sand.
